markers.impact: Altered glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity / HPA-axis stress response
markers.interpretation: The FKBP5 rs1360780 T allele has been associated in some studies with FKBP5 induction and differences in stress-response biology, especially in particular exposure contexts. It is not a prediction of PTSD, depression, or behavior.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Epigenetic changes (methylation of FKBP5) driven by early-life stress are the primary molecular switch.

sources.name: FKBP5 gene-environment interactions and HPA axis
sources.notes: Seminal study detailing T allele association with HPA axis hyper-responsiveness.

markers.interpretation: The HTR2A A-1438G A allele has been studied for its potential to increase serotonin 2A receptor density. It is evaluated as a research-grade marker for emotional reactivity and atypical responses to serotonergic drugs.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Promoter activity varies widely based on localized cellular factors and epigenetic methylation state.

sources.name: HTR2A promoter polymorphism expression studies
sources.notes: Shows modest impact of A allele on receptor promoter activity.

markers.impact: Altered oxytocin receptor sensitivity / social stress buffering
markers.interpretation: The OXTR rs53576 A allele is studied in relation to social-emotional traits. A-carriers (AA/AG) may experience reduced oxytocin receptor sensitivity, affecting social support seeking and stress buffering under pressure.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Oxytocin dynamics are heavily modulated by early maternal bonding, social environment, and vasopressin pathways.

sources.name: OXTR polymorphism and emotional reactivity
sources.notes: Explores how the AA/AG genotypes buffer social stress less effectively.

markers.impact: Lower monoamine oxidase A enzyme activity
markers.interpretation: MAOA helps break down dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine. The rs6323 T allele has been associated with lower enzyme activity in some studies and may be linked to greater emotional reactivity under acute stress; effects vary with sex-chromosome status, environment, and context.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: MAOA is X-linked. Hemizygous males carrying the low-activity allele are affected much more strongly than heterozygous females.

sources.name: MAOA activity polymorphism and emotional regulation
sources.notes: Discusses interactions of low-activity MAOA with childhood environment.

markers.impact: Common COMT enzyme-activity context; not a brain dopamine measurement
markers.interpretation: COMT Val158Met has measurable effects on enzyme activity in some tissues and has been studied for cognition and stress response, but behavioral associations vary across studies and context. A consumer SNP does not measure prefrontal dopamine, diagnose ADHD or anxiety, or predict stimulant response.
confirm_with: current attention, mood, and sleep symptoms
clinical assessment when symptoms affect daily life
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Cell type, sex hormones, environment, and many other factors shape COMT activity. Common genotype does not measure neurotransmitter levels or establish a 'warrior/worrier' personality type.

sources.name: COMT Val158Met impact on cognition and stress
sources.notes: Seminal review paper on Val158Met 'worrier vs. warrior' evolutionary tradeoff.

markers.impact: Candidate research on a dopamine-receptor-region variant; receptor density is not inferable
markers.interpretation: TaqIA is located in ANKK1 near DRD2. It has been studied for possible differences in dopamine D2 receptor binding, but findings do not support estimating an individual’s receptor density, reward behavior, ADHD status, or treatment response from this consumer marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This older candidate marker is not a clinical test. Published group-level binding estimates are not individual measurements and should not be presented as a personal percentage.

sources.name: ANKK1 TaqIA and dopamine D2 receptor binding
sources.notes: Older PET candidate-gene study of group-level receptor binding; it does not establish an individual receptor-density estimate or ADHD/reward-behavior prediction.

markers.impact: Synonymous DRD2 variant studied in exploratory receptor and cognition research
markers.interpretation: DRD2 C957T is a synonymous variant studied for possible effects on mRNA stability and receptor binding. Associations with cognition or receptor availability are exploratory and inconsistent; this consumer SNP does not establish working-memory ability, a cognitive disorder, or medication response.
confirm_with: reported cognitive concerns and functional impact
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Candidate-gene findings do not yield a clinical measure of receptor abundance or a dependable prediction of cognition.

sources.name: DRD2 C957T effects on translation and mRNA stability
sources.notes: Demonstrates structural mRNA stability changes caused by synonymous variant.

markers.impact: Neurodevelopmental cell adhesion / sensory processing traits
markers.interpretation: CNTNAP2 is involved in neural migration and synaptic development. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to language development variation, sensory processing, and autism spectrum traits.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Extremely weak statistical odds ratio; not diagnostic for any neurodevelopmental condition.

sources.name: CNTNAP2 and language processing in the general population
sources.notes: Examines association with developmental language profiles.

markers.interpretation: MSNP1AS regulates neuronal structure. The T allele represents a minor research-level susceptibility variant replicated in broad neurodevelopmental studies, showing weak statistical correlation with autism spectrum traits.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Non-diagnostic common variant with very low penetrance.

sources.name: MSNP1AS expression changes in autism cerebral cortex
sources.notes: Analyzes how this non-coding RNA affects cell adhesion markers.

markers.impact: Altered prefrontal alpha-2A adrenergic receptor tone
markers.interpretation: ADRA2A encodes the alpha-2A adrenergic receptor. This promoter variant has appeared in candidate studies of methylphenidate response, but it is not a validated pharmacogenomic test and cannot diagnose ADHD or predict whether a medication will work.
confirm_with: prescriber review of observed benefit and adverse effects
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Candidate response findings are not sufficient for medication selection; use clinical assessment and observed response with a prescriber.

sources.name: ADRA2A polymorphism and methylphenidate response
sources.notes: Candidate study in children with ADHD; do not interpret as a validated or individual medication-response test.

markers.interpretation: The ESR1 Pvull G allele is a research-grade marker associated with altered transcriptional activity of estrogen receptor alpha, investigated in studies of mood fluctuations during rapid hormone drops.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Hormone sensitivity is a complex neurobiological trait involving estrogen receptor complexing, progesterone balance, and central GABAA receptors.

sources.name: ESR1 polymorphisms and premenstrual dysphoric symptoms
sources.notes: Investigates estrogen receptor variants and luteal mood patterns.

markers.impact: Estrogen receptor splicing / binding affinity variation
markers.interpretation: ESR1 rs2234693 regulates receptor splicing. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to estrogen signaling sensitivity and emotional/physical symptoms during estrogen withdrawal.
confirm_with: symptoms of estrogen dominance or withdrawal
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Replication in PMDD is restricted to candidate-gene studies; GWAS results show highly polygenic etiology.

sources.name: Estrogen receptor alpha gene (ESR1) and mood regulation
sources.notes: Details splicing variance in response to estrogen concentration shifts.

markers.interpretation: PGR rs8079626 A-carriers are evaluated in research regarding progesterone receptor sensitivity. Linked to mood fluctuations during the luteal progesterone spike.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Progesterone's neuroactive metabolite (allopregnanolone) acts directly on GABAA receptors; PGR sequence is only part of the pathway.

sources.name: PGR variants and progesterone sensitivity in mood disorders
sources.notes: Finds mild association with adverse progesterone effects.

markers.interpretation: The Met66 (A) allele reduces the activity-dependent release of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor, which regulates synaptic plasticity and neurogenesis. Associated with alterations in episodic memory, working memory, and plasticity response to aerobic exercise.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Overall BDNF levels are highly modifiable by exercise, environmental enrichment, heat shock (sauna), and dietary polyphenols.

sources.name: BDNF Val66Met polymorphism impact on brain plasticity
sources.notes: Key paper establishing secretion defects of the Met66 variant.

markers.impact: Increased anandamide levels / reduced FAAH expression
markers.interpretation: FAAH degrades anandamide (the bliss molecule). The Thr129 (A) allele reduces enzyme activity, leading to elevated baseline anandamide. Associated with lower baseline anxiety, faster fear extinction, and decreased stress sensitivity.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Synonymous genetic background; other cannabinoid receptor variants (CNR1) modulate the actual endocannabinoid tone.

sources.name: FAAH Pro129Thr and anxiety phenotypes
sources.notes: Documents reduction in FAAH protein expression and increased drug/alcohol abuse protection.

markers.impact: Altered adenosine receptor sensitivity / caffeine anxiety risk
markers.interpretation: The T allele of rs5751876 is associated with increased susceptibility to caffeine-induced anxiety. Caffeine blocks ADORA2A receptors; carriers of the risk allele experience heightened sympathetic stimulation and panic responses.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Interacts closely with CYP1A2 clearance velocity; fast metabolizers clear caffeine before anxiety spikes.

sources.name: ADORA2A and caffeine anxiety
sources.notes: Establishes genetic link between adenosine receptor variants and panic sensitivity.

markers.impact: Altered mu-opioid receptor binding affinity / reward sensitivity
markers.interpretation: The G (Asp) allele changes the mu-opioid receptor sequence and has mixed, small-effect associations with pain- and reward-related traits across studies. It is not a prediction of pain sensitivity, attachment, or behavior.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Epigenetic endorphin feedback loops are heavily dependent on environmental social stress.

sources.name: OPRM1 A118G and opioid receptor expression
sources.notes: Demonstrates reduction in receptor mRNA levels in G allele carriers.

markers.impact: Reduced dopamine beta-hydroxylase expression / lower norepinephrine
markers.interpretation: The DBH -1021C>T promoter T allele reduces the conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine. Homozygous T/T carriers have significantly lower plasma DBH activity, shifting dopamine-norepinephrine ratios in stress circuits.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Norepinephrine release is heavily buffered by cellular adrenal output and MAO-A clearance rates.

sources.name: DBH promoter polymorphism and plasma activity
sources.notes: Confirms -1021C>T explains up to 35-50% of the variance in circulating DBH activity.

markers.impact: Prevents psychiatric/personality overcalling from common SNPs
markers.interpretation: Single common neuropsych variants must not be used to diagnose depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, addiction, personality disorders, empathy level, intelligence, trauma response, or medication outcome. They also do not measure brain neurotransmitter levels or justify choosing a medication or supplement. Treat common markers as weak pathway research only.
do_not_claim: neurotransmitter deficiency from a common SNP
supplement indication from a common SNP
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Psychiatric and behavioral traits are highly polygenic and environment-sensitive; candidate-gene literature has a high false-positive history. A consumer array cannot measure neurotransmitter levels or identify a supplement need.
